title: Divorce by Mutual Consent — Section 28 SMA

content.overview: Section 28 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides for divorce by mutual consent. The parties must have been living separately for a period of one year or more, must not have been able to live together, and must have mutually agreed that the marriage should be dissolved. The ordinary second-motion interval is six to eighteen months; any waiver analysis must be approached carefully and is not automatic.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Joint petition? (2) One year separate living? (3) Unable to live together? (4) Mutual agreement? (5) Second motion timing?
content.study:
s. 28 is the mutual-consent path; s. 27 is contested.

Case already in migrated file: Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017) 8 SCC 746 — cooling-off period treated as directory with waiver in appropriate circumstances under the analogous HMA provision; SMA application requires careful statutory analysis. No additional cases invented.

hypotheticals.question: Is the cooling-off period always mandatory under SMA s. 28?
hypotheticals.analysis: The ordinary interval is six to eighteen months; any waiver must be approached on the applicable jurisprudential basis and is not automatic. Amardeep Singh concerned HMA s. 13B(2); apply to SMA with careful statutory analysis.

misconceptions.trap: Cooling-off can always be skipped at will.
misconceptions.correction: Waiver is not automatic; approach on the applicable jurisprudential basis with careful statutory analysis.

cases.issue: Whether the cooling-off period is mandatory or directory and when it may be waived.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Court treated the analogous HMA cooling-off period as directory and recognized waiver in appropriate circumstances; decision directly concerned HMA s. 13B(2), so SMA application requires careful statutory analysis.
cases.holding: Cooling-off directory with waiver in appropriate cases under the HMA provision considered.
